newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says ETA political wing threatened judge.
newsitem.headline: Spain says ETA political wing threatened judge.

text.p: Spanish Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said on Thursday the political arm of Basque separatist group ETA had threatened a Supreme Court judge in an attempt to avoid prosecution.

The leadership of ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna has been charged in the Supreme Court with distributing an illegal video promoting the Basque guerrilla group during Spain's 1996 election campaign.
"(Herri Batasuna) has threatened in an intolerable way one of the court's members because it is afraid and is trying to avoid a particular sentence," Mayor Oreja said.

Supreme Court Judge Jose Manuel Martinez Pereda has summoned 23 members of Herri Batasuna's leadership on May 28 to inform them of their upcoming trial. They were arrested in February and spent two months in jail before posting bail.

"Herri Batasuna denounces this action of persecution against it by the Supreme Court," the party said in a statement on Wednesday. It branded Martinez an "ultra-rightist" and said he was motivated by revenge in his desire to jail them.

In the past, similar denouncements by Herri Batasuna have been closely followed by ETA attacks. ETA has targeted members of the judiciary before and assassinated a Supreme Court judge in Madrid earlier this year.
ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, has killed some 800 people in a nearly 30-year struggle for an independent state encompassing parts of northern Spain and southern France.
